boundaries: Five metadata-selected sources; probes are dependent within source
Nominal depths use delivered PSF flux and an adopted spatial profile
Recovery requires the correct clock, at least three observed events and significance under both block-null calibrations
Conditional surrogate false alarms do not establish survey reliability
Compare arms within this run; the earlier pilot used shorter spans and a different source-flux calibration
Delivered PSF has observed-noise measurements only; its adaptive extraction was not replayed
No physical photon limit, discovery, validation or detector adoption follows from this pilot
conclusions: Some usable information remains in the pixels: a Q1 deep-signal gain exceeds the mission-only arm.
No demonstrated recovery gain at 40-1000 ppm in this five-source pilot.
Production recovery at 1000 ppm is 1/5 in every arm; at 3000 ppm it is 3/5 SAP, 4/5 pixels, 4/5 mission-only.
The production endpoint demonstrates no pixel-specific recovery gain at the tested depths.
The 1000 ppm controlled-search count difference is a frozen clock-matching boundary; all three arms detect that example significantly.
No extraction or detector adoption follows. The nominal white-noise screen remains conditional, not a physical detection ceiling.

protocol.span: All supplied common full-quarter native cadences
protocol.detector: Unchanged selected production design; 0.5/1d biweight and3d physical knots
protocol.error: Same original aperture diagonal error for every arm; detector noise estimation unchanged
protocol.injection: Delivered PSF median times primary moving spatial profile; refit both adaptive arms after every raw-pixel injection
protocol.controls: Original curve and two positive controls per source and arm
protocol.limits: Positive-control endpoint check, not false-alarm calibration or programme gate

boundaries: Single nominal-profile clock at 1000 and 3000 ppm; no native 10000 ppm run.
Original curves are descriptive controls, not a production false-alarm calibration.
Unchanged production preparation can select different cadence masks by arm; masks and support are saved and independently checked.
The extra Q2 recovery has identical support across arms and is shared with mission-only processing.

processing_boundaries: Start from calibrated exposure-integrated Kepler TPF pixels, not individual photon arrivals or a fresh RAW_CNTS calibration.
Mission calibration and delivered KBonus background convention remain fixed; every adaptive step in the added pixel correction is refit.
Four published KBonus profiles and one explicitly weaker Q1 mission PRF; source flux from delivered corrected PSF median.
No replay of the original multi-TPF KBonus PSF/background pipeline.
Delivered PSF is an observed-noise benchmark only, not a pixel-refitted injection-recovery arm.
Held nulls are conditional block-sign surrogates; neither their rates nor five-source recovery estimates establish survey performance.
